cards.title: Wallpaper Picker UI
cards.description: A lightweight desktop application for browsing and applying wallpapers, designed for low resource usage and deep system integration. Media processing and thumbnail generation powered by FFmpeg, with multilingual i18n support.

paragraphs: Wallpaper Picker UI is a lightweight Linux desktop application for browsing, previewing, and applying static or animated wallpapers, with a particular focus on dynamic wallpapers through mpvpaper. The application provides a clean thumbnail-based interface, automatic video thumbnail generation with FFmpeg, and customizable wallpaper commands, allowing it to adapt to different setups and automation workflows.

Built with Tauri 2, the application combines a Svelte and TypeScript frontend with a Rust backend for native system integration while maintaining low resource usage. It also uses Tauri's capability-based permission system to restrict filesystem access, allowing the application to access only its own configuration file and thumbnail cache.

The interface includes custom and preset themes, manual light and dark mode switching, multilingual support, and automatic updates. FFmpeg handles media processing and thumbnail generation, while mpvpaper provides the recommended backend for animated wallpapers.

cards.title: Kanatype
cards.description: A lightweight desktop application for learning and practicing Hiragana, Katakana, and Kanji through interactive exercises, character filters, and a reference table.

paragraphs: Kanatype is a desktop application focused on learning and practicing Japanese characters, offering separate or combined practice modes for Hiragana, Katakana, and Kanji.

The application features an interactive interface with immediate feedback, intelligent character filters, and a reference table for quick lookup. It also includes light and dark themes and a responsive interface.

Built with Tauri 2, the project combines a React, TypeScript, and Vite frontend with a Rust backend, providing a lightweight application with native system integration and a capability-based permission model.

cards.title: matuz.dev
cards.description: This very site — a bilingual portfolio built as an SPA with its own design system, restrained editorial motion, and a fully tested component library.

paragraphs: This site is itself one of my projects: a bilingual (pt-BR / English) React SPA built around its own design system — display serif headings, mono micro-labels, and a restrained blue-violet palette — along with centralized animation presets that respect prefers-reduced-motion.

Everything is composed from a folder-per-component library with colocated tests and barrel exports, covering layout primitives, UI blocks, and content cards. The notes system fetches Markdown at runtime from a private Obsidian vault through an Express API with a secure token and renders callouts, mathematics, syntax highlighting, and more.
The test suite runs more than 230 tests with Vitest and Testing Library, while CI blocks every push on linting, tests, and production builds. You're looking at the demo right now.

cards.title: Cinema Automation Challenge - Robot Framework
cards.description: A test automation challenge for a cinema application, built to practice and demonstrate advanced web test automation using Robot Framework with Browser Library.

paragraphs: A test automation challenge for a cinema web application, structured around a keyword-driven architecture: test suites, reusable keyword resources, and environment variables are cleanly separated. Authentication flows (registration, login, logout, profile) and booking flows (movie search, showtimes, seat selection, checkout) are covered with positive, negative, validation, and smoke tags for selective execution.

The suite uses Browser Library (Playwright) for web automation and FakerLibrary for dynamic test data generation. Every test, keyword, and suite is fully documented, while execution produces HTML reports, detailed logs, and automatic screenshots on failures.

This project demonstrates layered test architecture, code reuse through shared keywords, parameterized keywords with optional arguments, tag-based organization, and robust error handling — practices I bring to any automation project.
